checks.why: a handler written as `const listAdmins = catchAsync(async (req, res) => …)` is a const, not a method, so the route wording the method target gets never applied: the registration `router.get('/admins', listAdmins)` was printed as '[by name] … reads it'. The const's declaration hands a function to the wrapper and the route line hands one to the router, both engine edges
the same when the const is declared in the file that registers it: the read was [in scope] and still not a route

a file:line on a const targets the const. It used to resolve to the enclosing <module> (other.js:2) or to the arrow in the initializer (adminController.js:2), so a const could only be asked by its bare name, which answers for every const so named
and a file that declares its own const of the name reads its own, not the wrapped handler's: other.js's `['root']` is not a reader of the controller's listAdmins
CONTROL: a plain function handler keeps the wording it already had, from the method rule
CONTROL: `const arrowAdmins = async (req, res) => …` IS the function, so its file:line stays the method, with the method's route row
CONTROL: a const that holds a value, read inside an inline handler on a route line, is a read — the inline arrow hands nothing over and the const's initializer is not a function
the handler read through its module (`.get(auth(), adminController.listAdmins)` after `.route(…)`) is registered there too: it was '[by name] … writes/reads it'

a chained registration split over lines (`router\n  .route('/admins-c')\n  .get(auth(), adminController.listAdmins)`) records its hand-off on the statement's first line and names the handler two lines down: registered there too
a service that declares its own function of the name reads its own in its exports, not the controller's const
a file:line in a file whose name carries a dot (`report.controller.js`) is a file and a line: the dots were read as a package prefix and every such target was refused
CONTROL: a file:line in a file that is not in the graph is still refused
the registered row claims the hand-off edge on the route line, so `verified:` finds it: it printed '✗ 1 not found' for every such row
`router.route('/reports').get(listReports)` is a GET route: the `route` call on the same line named the method ROUTE
a chain registering two methods on one line names both: a reference records a line, not the argument list it sat in

a handler wrapped by a LIBRARY (`asyncHandler` from a package) has no engine edge for what the wrapper returns, so the row keeps the name's rung but says what the line does: it was '[by name] … reads it'
want: [by name] lib.<module>   src/routes/lib.js:5   — registered as a GET route "/lib"

checks.why: CONTROL: a line that also hands over a plain function (`.post(libList, plainAdmins)`) is not evidence for the const: the hand-off is plainAdmins', so the const's row stays [by name]
want: [by name] lib.<module>   src/routes/lib.js:6   — registered as a POST route "/lib-mixed"

checks.why: CONTROL: a const holding a module (`const adminController = require(…)`) read on a route line is read there, not registered
CONTROL: a qualified read of a const holding a value, off any route line, stays a read
